title: Diagnose silent worker post-flight auto-commit failure
description: All of 2026-07-31 the fleet completed tasks into REVIEW/DONE but the moe-agent wrapper post-flight never committed or pushed (autoCommit defaults on, no qualityGate set, branch was moe/work-2026-07-31 so branch-safety should pass, no PUSH-BLOCKED chat messages). A human session landed everything manually. Reproduce: run a worker via the JetBrains Agents menu on a task that reaches REVIEW; capture wrapper stdout; find why the auto-commit path is skipped or failing silently. Fix + add a chat escalation when the commit step errors.
definitionOfDone: root cause identified with wrapper log evidence
auto-commit fires on REVIEW in a live run (commit visible in git log)
silent-failure path now posts a chat warning
postflight harness test covers the regression

implementationPlan.description: CONFIRM THE ROOT CAUSE WITH HARD EVIDENCE — do not take the planning notes on faith. (a) Count the corpus: `ls .moe/tasks/*.json | wc -l` (expected ~257). (b) Reproduce the truncation directly: `bash scripts/moe-call.sh list_tasks '{}' --project D:/projexts/moes` and assert the returned `tasks` array length is exactly 100 while `pagination.total` reports the true count — that single response IS the bug. (c) Pick a task that recently reached REVIEW or DONE (e.g. one of the epic-2eb35551 splits) and confirm its id is ABSENT from that 100-row page, proving the wrapper's `Where-Object { $_.id -eq $preflightTaskId }` would match nothing. (d) Re-read moe-agent.ps1 around lines 2026-2110 and moe-agent.sh around 2626-2700 and confirm the control flow: an empty status makes the `-eq "REVIEW"` test false and the whole block — including every Write-Host diagnostic and the PUSH-BLOCKED chat escalation — is skipped without a single line of output. (e) Confirm the installed plugin's copy is still byte-identical: `diff -q scripts/moe-agent.ps1 "$APPDATA/JetBrains/PyCharm2026.1/plugins/moe-jetbrains/scripts/moe-agent.ps1"`. If it now DIFFERS, stop and re-derive — you would be fixing different code than the fleet runs (mem:moes-installed-plugin-staleness). (f) Record all of this verbatim; the first DoD item is 'root cause identified with wrapper log evidence' and this transcript is that evidence.
implementationPlan.note:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED — and the planning note is HALF WRONG. Two independent defects; only the second explains 2026-07-31.

(a) Corpus: `ls .moe/tasks/*.json | wc -l` = 257 (137 status=ARCHIVED, so listTasks' true active total is 120).

(b) TRUNCATION REPRODUCED (defect A, real + live): `bash scripts/moe-call.sh list_tasks '{}' --project D:/projexts/moes` returns `tasks.length = 100` against `pagination = {"limit":100,"offset":0,"returned":100,"total":120,"hasMore":true}`. Re-verified through a byte-faithful PowerShell replica of Invoke-MoeRpc (ps1:936-1002) + the post-flight lookup (ps1:2029-2058): `listResp.tasks count : 100`. 20 active tasks — all DONE, orders 15-60 — are absent from page 1 (global ascending sort by `order` puts the highest-order tasks off the end).

(c) BUT the truncation is NOT what broke the fleet. All 8 tasks that reached DONE on 2026-07-31 (task-1bc9d7a8, task-db4091d0, task-5c824346, task-aa44c1be, task-aa88d8e8, task-cec5c669, task-f05cbea9, task-f56df322) have order 1-10 and were verified PRESENT in the returned page by set membership. The `Where-Object { $_.id -eq $preflightTaskId }` filter WOULD have matched. The planning note's causal claim does not hold on this box.

(d) THE ACTUAL CAUSE (defect B): the post-flight block is never reached for workers, because the wrapper is still blocked inside the CLI call.
  - `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process`: PID 23104 = `moe-agent.ps1 -Role worker ... -Command 'claude' -Team 'moes' -Interactive` (alive since 15:42Z); PID 28492 = same for worker-5c53582f; PID 52412 = `-Role qa ... -Team 'moes'` with NO -Interactive.
  - `TerminalAgentLauncher.kt:384 shouldLaunchClaudeInteractive` returns true for architect/worker/governor, false for qa. Its own KDoc: "Worker: always — hands-on coding sessions want the TUI." This contradicts CLAUDE.md ("worker/qa to one-shot").
  - ps1:1888 `$usePrintMode = -not $Interactive` -> worker launches the full claude TUI at ps1:2002 and the wrapper blocks there for the TUI's entire human-driven lifetime. `Invoke-PostFlight` (2024) and the whole auto-commit block (2026) are strictly downstream.
  - CHAT EVIDENCE (whole history, all channels): 13 `qa session ended: task=… (CLI exit=0)` messages, and ZERO `worker session ended` / `architect session ended`. The two roles launched -Interactive are exactly the two that have never once emitted a post-flight signal. `git log` confirms every commit on moe/work-2026-07-31 is human-authored (yaront1111).
  - Isolated by controlled harness (fake proxy, FAKE_TASK_STATUS=REVIEW, instantly-exiting fake CLI): MODE=print -> commits=2, session-ended msg True, 'Post-flight: auto-commit' True; MODE=interactive -> commits=2, session-ended True, auto-commit True. The code path is fine in BOTH modes when the CLI returns — which isolates the failure to the real TUI not returning.
  - Also proved chat_send is not the failure: a live proxy probe as worker-f5977052 to chan-b6d8273b returned success:true.

Control flow re-read and confirmed: ps1:2036 `Invoke-MoeRpc -Tool "list_tasks" -Args @{}` -> null `$matched` -> `$finalStatus` stays $null -> the `-eq "REVIEW"` test at 2068 is false -> every Write-Host, the branch-safety messages and the PUSH-BLOCKED escalation (all INSIDE the block) are skipped with zero output. sh:2629 `moe_rpc list_tasks '{}'` feeding `[ "$FINAL_STATUS" = "REVIEW" ]` at 2682 is the identical defect. Second instance in the same block: `siblingMax`/`epic_final` is computed off the same truncated page.

(e) `diff -q` vs %APPDATA%\JetBrains\PyCharm2026.1\plugins\moe-jetbrains\scripts\: IDENTICAL for both moe-agent.ps1 and moe-agent.sh — no installed-plugin drift confounding this; repo fixes are directly testable but still need buildPlugin + reinstall to reach the fleet.

implementationPlan.description: MAKE THE HARNESS CATCH IT — write the failing test BEFORE the fix, or you cannot prove the fix works. In scripts/tests/postflight.sh, the fake proxy's `case 'list_tasks'` stub (~line 105) unconditionally returns `task-postflight`, which is exactly why a green harness coexisted with a completely inert production auto-commit path. Add a `FAKE_LIST_TASKS_TRUNCATED=1` mode that makes the list_tasks stub return a page that OMITS task-postflight (return an unrelated filler row or an empty array) while `get_context` keeps returning the real task — this models the daemon paginating the task off the end. Add a test case that runs the wrapper in that mode with FAKE_TASK_STATUS=REVIEW and asserts a commit WAS created. Run it now and watch it FAIL against the current wrapper: that failure is the regression reproduced in CI-able form, and a test that passes before the fix proves nothing. Mirror the same mode and case in scripts/tests/postflight.ps1 so both platforms are covered. Do not modify any existing assertion in either harness while you are in there.
implementationPlan.note:
Failing tests written BEFORE the fix, in both harnesses. No existing assertion touched.

Fake-proxy stub changes (identical in .sh and .ps1):
- `get_context` now returns a full task (status from FAKE_TASK_STATUS, plus reopenCount/epicId/order) instead of just id+plan, so the exact-lookup fix has something to read. New `FAKE_GET_CONTEXT_FAIL=1` mode returns `{}` (daemon answered, no task).
- `list_tasks` split by scope: an epic-SCOPED call (args.epicId present) always answers in full; the UNSCOPED call honours new `FAKE_LIST_TASKS_TRUNCATED=1` by returning a single unrelated filler row plus a `pagination` block with hasMore:true — modelling DEFAULT_TASK_LIST_LIMIT paginating task-postflight off the end. The old stub returned task-postflight unconditionally, which is exactly why a green harness coexisted with a dead production auto-commit path.

New cases (both harnesses):
- Case 5 truncation: FAKE_LIST_TASKS_TRUNCATED=1 + FAKE_TASK_STATUS=REVIEW, gate disabled -> asserts 2 commits (auto-commit fired).
- Case 6 lookup failure: FAKE_GET_CONTEXT_FAIL=1 + REVIEW -> asserts stdout carries `post-flight status lookup failed for task task-postflight` AND chan-general.jsonl carries `PUSH-BLOCKED: post-flight status lookup failed for task task-postflight`.

RED as required, and the pre-existing cases all pass first (the run reaches Case 5 only after resume/one-shot-argv/interactive/heartbeat/gate-fail/gate-pass/gate-skip/gate-midepic have all gone green):

implementationPlan.description: FIX THE POWERSHELL WRAPPER. In scripts/moe-agent.ps1, replace the truncatable status lookup at ~line 2036 with an exact one. (a) Swap `Invoke-MoeRpc -Tool "list_tasks" -Args @{}` for `Invoke-MoeRpc -Tool "get_context" -Args @{ taskId = $preflightTaskId }`, reading `$resp.task.status`, `$resp.task.reopenCount` and `$resp.task.epicId` off the returned task. get_context keys on the task id and cannot be paginated away — that is the entire point. Do NOT 'fix' this by passing `limit = 500` instead: MAX_TASK_LIST_LIMIT is 500, so that silently re-breaks past 500 tasks and reproduces this exact defect at a higher threshold. (b) Fix the second instance of the same bug in the same block: `$isEpicFinal` currently computes `siblingMax` from the truncated page, so it can misjudge a mid-epic task as epic-final (running the full quality gate on it) or skip the gate on the true final task. Recompute it from an epic-SCOPED call — `list_tasks` with `@{ epicId = $taskEpicId; limit = 500 }` — which is legitimately bounded because it asks about one epic's siblings. (c) ADD THE MISSING ERROR HANDLING, which is the actual defect: today a failed or empty lookup is indistinguishable from 'the task genuinely is not in REVIEW' and both exit in total silence. Separate them. If the lookup throws or returns no task, emit a `[WARN]` line naming the task id and the reason, AND post a chat escalation (reuse the PUSH-BLOCKED message plumbing, wording it as a status-lookup failure) so the skip is never again invisible. A genuine non-REVIEW status stays a quiet no-op — that one is correct behavior. (d) Keep the whole path best-effort: a lookup failure must warn and continue, never abort the wrapper loop. (e) Do not add any new `2>&1 |` merge near the git calls — lines 2106-2109 document that native git writes progress to stderr on SUCCESS and $ErrorActionPreference='Stop' turns that into a terminating NativeCommandError.
implementationPlan.note:
scripts/moe-agent.ps1 post-flight status lookup rewritten (was ps1:2036-2058).

(a) `Invoke-MoeRpc -Tool "list_tasks" -Args @{}` + client-side `Where-Object { $_.id -eq $preflightTaskId }` replaced by `Invoke-MoeRpc -Tool "get_context" -Args @{ taskId = $preflightTaskId }`, reading status/reopenCount/epicId/order off `$ctxResp.task`. Guarded on `$ctxResp.task.id` so an empty `{}` response is detected rather than silently yielding a null status. NOT fixed with `limit = 500` — comment in place stating MAX_TASK_LIST_LIMIT is 500 and raising the bound only moves the same silent cliff.

(b) `$isEpicFinal`/`$siblingMax` no longer read the truncated page. They now come from an epic-SCOPED `list_tasks @{ epicId = ...; limit = 500 }`, so the `Where-Object { $_.epicId -eq ... }` client-side filter is gone with it. A bound is legitimate here because the collection asked about is one epic's siblings, not the whole project.

(c) New error handling, kept strictly distinct from a genuine non-REVIEW status. Lookup throw or no-task now sets `$statusLookupError`, which emits `[WARN] post-flight status lookup failed for task <id>: <reason>...` on stdout AND posts a `PUSH-BLOCKED: post-flight status lookup failed for task <id> (<reason>)` chat message through the same `$generalChannelId` + Invoke-MoeRpc chat_send plumbing the qualityGate failure uses. A real non-REVIEW status stays a quiet no-op, which is correct behaviour.

(d) Best-effort preserved: both the get_context call and the chat_send are inside try/catch, the epic-scoped sibling call has its own try/catch defaulting `$isEpicFinal = $true`, and no path throws or `break`s — the wrapper loop continues.

(e) No new `2>&1 |` merge anywhere near the git calls; the git block and its $ErrorActionPreference='Continue' guard are untouched.

Verified: `scripts/tests/postflight.ps1` now exits 0 with "PASS postflight.ps1". The two cases added in step-2 flipped from RED to GREEN and every pre-existing case still passes.

implementationPlan.description: FIX THE BASH WRAPPER TO MATCH — both or neither. scripts/moe-agent.sh has the identical defect at line 2629 (`POSTFLIGHT_STATE=$(moe_rpc list_tasks '{}' ...)`) feeding the `[ "$FINAL_STATUS" = "REVIEW" ]` test at line 2682. Apply the same three changes: exact `get_context` lookup keyed on $PREFLIGHT_TASK_ID for status/reopenCount/epicId; epic-scoped `list_tasks` with an explicit epicId and limit for the epic-final computation; and the warn-plus-chat-escalation error handling path when the lookup fails or comes back empty, distinct from a genuine non-REVIEW status. This is not optional parity work: the JetBrains launcher picks .ps1 or .sh by platform and WSL agent mode ALWAYS uses .sh, so fixing only PowerShell leaves every Linux, macOS and WSL fleet silently broken with no signal. Match the existing bash idioms in the file — note the current code parses the RPC response with a `read -r -d $'\x1f'` field split (~line 2664); keep whatever parsing style the surrounding code uses rather than introducing a new one. Preserve the `2>/dev/null || echo ""` best-effort posture on the RPC call itself, but make the EMPTY result now take the loud path instead of falling through silently.
implementationPlan.note:
scripts/moe-agent.sh post-flight status lookup brought to parity with the .ps1 fix (was sh:2629-2668).

(a) `moe_rpc list_tasks '{}'` replaced by `moe_rpc get_context '{"taskId": ...}'`, with the taskId JSON built through the same `$PYTHON_CMD -c "import json,sys; print(json.dumps(...))"` idiom the file already uses for chat_send/add_comment rather than hand-rolled string interpolation. The python parser now reads `d.get('task')` and emits status/reopenCount/epicId/order, keeping the existing `\x1f`-separated `read -r -d $'\x1f'` field-split style; only the field list changed (epicId + order replace the precomputed epic_final). Guarded on `t.get('id')` so an empty `{}` response is detected instead of yielding a blank status.

(b) Epic-final is now computed from a separate epic-SCOPED `moe_rpc list_tasks '{"epicId": ..., "limit": 500}'` in its own small python block, so the client-side `s.get('epicId') == epic_id` filter over the truncated page is gone. Bounded legitimately: it asks about one epic's siblings, not the project.

(c) The `2>/dev/null || echo ""` best-effort posture on the RPC itself is preserved, but an EMPTY parse result no longer falls through silently — it sets STATUS_LOOKUP_ERROR, which prints `${YELLOW}[WARN]${NC} post-flight status lookup failed for task <id>: ...` and posts `PUSH-BLOCKED: post-flight status lookup failed for task <id> (<reason>)` to GENERAL_CHANNEL_ID via the same moe_rpc chat_send + json.dumps plumbing announce_gate_failure uses. A genuine non-REVIEW status stays a quiet no-op.

(d) Never aborts the loop: every RPC keeps `|| echo ""`, every python block keeps `2>/dev/null || echo <default>`, the chat_send keeps `|| true`, and there is no `exit`/`break` on this path. Semantically equivalent to the .ps1 version, field for field.

Verified: `bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh` -> SYNTAX OK; `bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh` -> exit 0, "PASS postflight.sh" (the truncation case that failed before the fix now passes, every pre-existing case still passes).

PARTIAL — read (e) below. Rebuild done, GUI live run NOT done. Also two real defects found by testing the fix against the LIVE daemon, both now fixed.

LIVE-DAEMON PROOF of the pagination fix (real daemon, not the fake proxy), on task-8caee725 (DONE, order 60, off page 1):
  OLD list_tasks @{}  -> returned 100 rows of 120 total; matched=False; finalStatus=''; WOULD AUTO-COMMIT=False

That is the silent skip and its fix, side by side, against production data.

TWO DEFECTS THE LIVE RUN EXPOSED IN MY OWN STEP-3/4 CODE (the fake-proxy stub had been lying about get_context's shape):
1. getContext.ts's task projection has NO epicId and NO order — it returns the resolved `epic` object alongside instead. Reading `task.epicId` would have silently disabled the mid-epic qualityGate deferral forever. Now: epicId comes from `$ctxResp.epic.id` / `d.get('epic')`, and this task's own `order` is read out of the epic-scoped sibling page (which is guaranteed to contain it, being scoped to its epic).
2. getContext.ts:53-60 falls back to the CALLER's `currentTaskId` when the requested id resolves to nothing, and moe-proxy injects MOE_WORKER_ID on every call — so a stale/deleted id answers with a DIFFERENT task. Verified live: get_context on 'task-does-not-exist-0000' returned task-321f3d51... (my own task, status WORKING). Auto-committing on another task's REVIEW would be worse than not committing. Both wrappers now require `task.id == $preflightTaskId` and route a mismatch to the loud path: "get_context resolved a different task (<id>) — the requested id no longer exists".
Harness stubs corrected to the real shapes (no epicId/order on task; `epic:{id}` alongside; FAKE_GET_CONTEXT_FAIL=empty|mismatch), and Case 7 added to both harnesses asserting the mismatch takes the loud path and does NOT commit. Re-verified: `bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh` -> PASS; `scripts/tests/postflight.ps1` -> PASS.

- Loud vs quiet are genuinely different paths, and now pinned by tests on BOTH sides: the failure cases assert the WARN + chat message, and a new assertion on the first (non-REVIEW) run asserts stdout does NOT contain 'post-flight status lookup failed'. Without that second assertion nothing stopped the quiet path from regressing into a warning.
- Cannot abort the loop: `sed -n '2029,2100p' scripts/moe-agent.ps1 | grep break/continue/exit/return/throw` -> only comment/string matches; the sh block's single `break` is inside the embedded python, not bash. ps1 wraps everything in try/catch (chat_send has its own), sh keeps `|| echo ""` / `|| echo "true"` / `|| true` on every RPC and python call.
- No new `2>&1 |` merge near git: `git diff -U0 -- scripts/moe-agent.ps1 | grep '^+' | grep -c '2>&1'` -> 0. The one added in .sh is `> /dev/null 2>&1 || true` on the chat_send RPC, the same idiom announce_gate_failure already uses, nowhere near the git calls (and bash has no NativeCommandError).
- The step-2 truncation test genuinely failed first: bash exited 1 on "A truncated list_tasks page must NOT stop the auto-commit ... (expected 2 commits)", ps1 exited 1 in gate-truncated. Independently, `git show HEAD:scripts/moe-agent.{ps1,sh} | grep -c "post-flight status lookup failed"` -> 0 for both, so the error-path assertions could not have been vacuously green either.

Extra finding while reviewing: the wrappers ALREADY default worker/qa to non-interactive (ps1:70, sh:349-362) — the TUI came purely from the launcher's explicit `-Interactive`. So the Kotlin fix needs no wrapper counterpart, and workers now also pick up the `CRITICAL (one-shot session)` prompt guard at ps1:1646. Corrected a stale comment at sh:349 that claimed bash "always runs in TUI regardless of this flag" — the harness proves bash passes `--print` for non-interactive roles — and replaced it with why the false default is load-bearing.

Known limitations, deliberately not changed (out of scope, flagged for QA): (1) the auto-commit still keys on REVIEW only, so if QA approves the task to DONE before the post-flight runs, the commit is skipped — the window is seconds under one-shot --print, but it is real under TURBO; (2) two workers finishing simultaneously still share one tree and one `git add -A` — pre-existing, untouched. Also note `.moe/tasks/task-8caee725.json` shows a `contextFetchedBy` diff: that is daemon-written state from the live-daemon diagnostic in step 6, not hand-editing.

Final verification, all fresh: `bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh` SYNTAX OK; `bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh` -> PASS postflight.sh (exit 0); `scripts/tests/postflight.ps1` -> PASS postflight.ps1 (exit 0); `cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test` -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL (exit 0).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Raise the limit: `list_tasks {limit: 500}`. REJECTED — MAX_TASK_LIST_LIMIT is 500, so this is a band-aid with a known ceiling that silently re-breaks past 500 tasks, reproducing the identical silent-skip class at a higher threshold. The whole defect is that an unbounded collection was queried with a bounded call. (2) Paginate through every page until the task is found. REJECTED — O(n) RPCs on every task completion to answer a single-key question. (3) CHOSEN: exact lookup via `get_context {taskId}`, which returns the task itself with status/reopenCount/epicId and cannot be truncated, then a SEPARATE epic-scoped `list_tasks {epicId, limit: 500}` for the epic-final computation, which is legitimately bounded because it asks about one epic's siblings. Also considered leaving the epic-final logic alone — rejected: it reads the same truncated page, so `siblingMax` is computed over whichever siblings happened to make page 1 and can misjudge a mid-epic task as epic-final (running the full quality gate on it) or the reverse (skipping the gate on the real final task). Same root cause, same block, fix both together.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: ROOT CAUSE FOUND STATICALLY BEFORE PLANNING — this is a confirm-and-fix, not an open hunt. Both wrappers look up the just-completed task's final status by listing EVERY task in the project and filtering client-side: moe-agent.ps1:2036 `Invoke-MoeRpc -Tool "list_tasks" -Args @{}` and moe-agent.sh:2629 `moe_rpc list_tasks '{}'`. The daemon (src/tools/listTasks.ts) defaults to DEFAULT_TASK_LIST_LIMIT (100), sorts with `[...tasks].sort((a, b) => a.order - b.order)` across ALL epics, and returns `sortedTasks.slice(offset, offset + limit)`. This project has **257 task files** in .moe/tasks/. Task `order` is a small per-epic number (1, 2, 3, 2.25…), so a global sort by order interleaves every epic and the first 100 rows are the lowest order values project-wide — whether any given completed task lands in that page is essentially arbitrary. When it does not: `$matched` is null, `$finalStatus` stays $null / FINAL_STATUS stays "", the `-eq "REVIEW"` test at ps1:2068 / sh:2682 is false, and the ENTIRE auto-commit block is skipped. Every diagnostic in that path — the 'Post-flight: auto-commit+push' line, the branch-safety messages, the PUSH-BLOCKED chat escalation — lives INSIDE the skipped branch, which is exactly why the failure was silent and why no PUSH-BLOCKED message ever appeared. Verified the installed plugin at %APPDATA%\JetBrains\PyCharm2026.1\plugins\moe-jetbrains\scripts\moe-agent.ps1 is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the repo copy (diff -q clean), so mem:moes-installed-plugin-staleness does not confound this one and repo fixes are directly testable — but the plugin still must be rebuilt+reinstalled for the fix to take effect on this box.
planningNotes.risks:
THE HARNESS CANNOT CURRENTLY CATCH THIS: scripts/tests/postflight.sh's fake proxy (the `case 'list_tasks'` stub, ~line 105) ALWAYS returns `task-postflight` in its response. The stub does not model pagination at all, which is precisely why a green harness coexisted with a totally inert auto-commit path in production. A regression test that does not first make the CURRENT wrapper fail proves nothing — add the truncation mode and watch it fail before fixing.
ERROR HANDLING IS THE ACTUAL DEFECT, not a nice-to-have: a failed/empty status lookup is currently indistinguishable from 'task legitimately is not in REVIEW', and both fall out of the block in silence. The fix must separate them — lookup failure is an ERROR that warns and escalates to chat; a genuine non-REVIEW status stays a quiet no-op. Collapsing them back together re-creates the bug with extra steps.
BOTH WRAPPERS OR NEITHER: the JetBrains launcher picks .ps1 or .sh by platform (and WSL agent mode always uses .sh). Fixing only PowerShell leaves every Linux/macOS/WSL fleet silently broken, and the divergence is invisible until someone runs the other platform.
PLUGIN REBUILD REQUIRED: the fleet runs the INSTALLED plugin's bundled scripts. They are byte-identical to the repo today, so the fix is inert on this box until `./gradlew buildPlugin` + `.\scripts\install-all.ps1` (mem:moes-installed-plugin-staleness). The DoD's 'live run' item cannot pass without it.
SHARED DIRTY TREE + THE BUG ITSELF: uncommitted fleet work is piled up in this tree precisely because of this defect. Do NOT `git add -A` and sweep it into your commit while testing the commit path — that is the failure mode this bug already caused once. Check `git status` before any live-run step and scope commits deliberately.
DO NOT EDIT INSTALLED PLUGIN FILES directly — that needs the user's explicit go-ahead; go through buildPlugin + install.
POWERSHELL STDERR TRAP: the script sets $ErrorActionPreference='Stop' and native git writes progress to stderr on SUCCESS; ps1:2106-2109 documents this. Any new `2>&1 |` merge you add near the git calls can turn benign stderr into a terminating NativeCommandError.
